Cluster gene sets

Source: R/clusterGeneSets.R
clusterGeneSets.Rd

Cluster gene sets

Usage

clusterGeneSets(
  geneSetsList,
  resolution = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.1, 1.6, 2.1, 2.6, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1),
  algorithm = "louvain",
  clusterArgs = list(),
  K = NA,
  elbow_method = "distance",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

geneSetsList

'gsList' object created with the 'initializeList()' function.

resolution

Vector with the desired clustering resolutions to use. Higher number usually results in more clusters.

algorithm

Clustering method applied to the SNN graph. Either the name of a registered method (see listClusterMethods(); e.g. 'louvain', 'leiden', 'slm', 'igraph_louvain', 'igraph_leiden', 'kmeans', 'apcluster', 'binary_cut'), a gsClusterMethod built with clusterMethod(), or a function following the same contract. Only this step is swappable – the SNN graph itself is always built the same way.

Methods that determine the number of clusters themselves ('kmeans', 'apcluster', 'binary_cut') ignore resolution and are run once; the result is stored under the first requested resolution.

clusterArgs

Named list of extra arguments passed on to the clustering method, for example list(n.start = 20) for the Seurat backends, list(maxK = 50) for 'kmeans', list(p = -1) for 'apcluster', or list(cutoff = 0.9) for 'binary_cut'.

K

Integer or NA. Number of nearest neighbors used when building the KNN graph. If NA (default) it is set to round(sqrt(N)), where N is the number of gene sets. Must be smaller than N.

elbow_method

Method for choosing the number of LSI dimensions from the scree curve: 'distance' (default) or 'zscore'. See the Details.

verbose

a logic indicating whether to print progress statements. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

'gsList' object with clustering stored. The best resolution (highest silhouette score) is annotated and used throughout the rest of the workflow (unless specified in subsequent functions).

Details

At least 10 gene sets are needed. The LSI uses up to 50 dimensions (fewer when there are 50 gene sets or less); the first one, which mostly reflects gene-set size, is always left out.

Clustering does not change the random number stream of the R session: the UMAP and the seeded clustering backends restore it afterwards. Re-clustering an object removes its existing labels, so run labelClusters() again afterwards.

See also

clusterMethod(), registerClusterMethod(), listClusterMethods()

Examples

geneSetsList <- initializeList(
  geneSetsList = exampleGeneSets,
  geneSetsDF = exampleEnrichment,
  verbose = FALSE
)
gsListObject <- clusterGeneSets(
  geneSetsList = geneSetsList,
  resolution = c(0.6, 1.1),
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Swap in a different community-detection implementation
gsListObject <- clusterGeneSets(
  geneSetsList,
  algorithm = "igraph_leiden",
  resolution = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
